The Prophet taught a desert Arab words of praise, and taught him and new Muslims to ask Allah for forgiveness, mercy, guidance, protection and provision.
Saying 'Hallowed be Allah' a hundred times records a thousand good deeds and wipes out a thousand sins each day.

Allah relieves whoever relieves a brother's distress, conceals the faults of one who conceals, eases Paradise's path for a seeker of knowledge, and sends tranquillity on gatherings studying the Quran.
Angels surround and mercy covers people sitting to remember Allah, and Gabriel told the Prophet that Allah spoke to the angels of the greatness of Companions sitting so.
The Prophet sought Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day and urged people to repent, and Allah accepts whoever repents before the sun rises from the west.
The Prophet told travellers shouting takbir that they call One All-Hearing and near, and taught that 'No might nor power but Allah' is a treasure of Paradise.
The Prophet taught Abu Bakr a supplication for his prayer, confessing great wrong to himself and asking Allah, the Forgiving and Compassionate, for pardon and mercy.
The Prophet sought refuge from the trials of Hell, the grave, wealth, poverty and the Dajjal, from sloth, cowardice, old age, miserliness and debt, and taught protective words against harm.
Going to bed, one should lie on the right side entrusting oneself to Allah, to die on the fitra if death comes; other bedtime words praise Allah and seek protection.
The Prophet sought refuge from the evil of what he had done and not done, in Allah's power from being led astray, and, setting out on journeys, from the Fire.
The Prophet asked forgiveness, the setting right of his religion, world and Hereafter, guidance, chastity and a purified soul, said evening and morning supplications, and taught Ali to seek guidance.
Four phrases of praise the Prophet said thrice outweighed Juwairiya's morning of devotion, and he taught Fatima, asking for a servant, to say takbir, tasbih and tahmid at bedtime.
Hearing a cock, ask Allah's favour, for it sees angels, and a donkey, seek refuge from Satan; in distress the Prophet affirmed Allah's oneness, Lord of the Throne.
The Prophet said the best words, chosen by Allah for His angels and servants and dearest to Him, are 'Hallowed be Allah and praise is due to Him'.
A Muslim's supplication for his brother in his absence is answered, and the commissioned angel says Amen, may it be for you too.
Allah is pleased with the servant who praises Him when he eats a morsel or takes a drink.
A supplication is answered as long as one does not ask for sin or cutting kinship and does not grow impatient, saying he prayed unanswered and giving up supplication.
The Prophet saw that most entering Paradise were poor, the wealthy held back, and most in the Fire were women, and said women would be a minority in Paradise.
The Prophet sought refuge in Allah from the loss of His blessing, the change of His protection, His sudden wrath and all His displeasure.
The Prophet said he left no trial more harmful to men than women; the world is sweet and green, so avoid women's allurement, which caused the Israelites' first trial.
Three men of earlier peoples, shut in a cave by a rock, invoked Allah by deeds done for Him: serving parents, sparing a cousin, repaying a labourer's grown wages.
Allah is more pleased with His servant's repentance than a traveller who, despairing in a waterless desert, finds his lost camel with its provisions.
Had people not sinned, Allah would have replaced them with people who sin, seek His forgiveness and are forgiven, as Abu Ayyub disclosed near his death.
Hanzala called himself a hypocrite for forgetting Paradise and Hell at home; the Prophet said angels would greet them if their remembrance lasted, but there is a time for each.
Allah's mercy prevails over His wrath; of its hundred parts He sent one to creation and kept ninety-nine for Resurrection, and is kinder to His servants than a mother.
A sinful man had his body burnt and scattered for fear of Allah, who gathered him and forgave him; a report adds a woman sent to Hell over a cat.
A servant who keeps sinning and asking forgiveness is forgiven, knowing his Lord forgives; Allah stretches His Hand night and day for repentance until the sun rises in the west.
None loves praise more than Allah, so He praised Himself, and none is more self-respecting, so He forbade abominations; He loves accepting excuses, so He sent the Book and Messengers.
For a man who kissed a woman a verse was revealed: pray, for good deeds remove misdeeds, for everyone; another seeking a prescribed punishment was pardoned for praying.
A killer of a hundred, a monk among them, died journeying in repentance to a land of pious people, and being nearer it was taken by the angels of mercy.
On Resurrection Day Allah would give each Muslim a Jew or Christian as rescue from Hell, forgiving heavy sins, and pardon a believer's concealed faults while exposing disbelievers and hypocrites.
Ka'b b. Malik recounted staying behind from Tabuk without excuse, telling the truth, being boycotted with two others fifty nights, until Allah revealed He accepted their repentance.
Ka'b b. Malik tells how he stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, told the Prophet the truth, was shunned fifty nights with two others, until Allah accepted their repentance.
Aisha tells of the false charge against her after she was left behind on a journey, her grief, the Prophet's consultations and address, and the verses revealing her innocence.
A man was charged with fornication with the Prophet's slave girl; told to strike his neck, Ali found the man's sexual organ cut off and refrained.
Revelation confirms Zaid b. Arqam against Abdullah b. Ubayy, whom at death the Prophet shrouds in his shirt and prays over despite Umar, before a verse forbids it.
Three persons by the House disputed whether Allah hears them when they speak loudly or in undertones, and the verse about ears, eyes and skins bearing witness was revealed.
When some turned back on the way to Uhud, the Companions split over killing them, and the verse asking why they were two parties over the hypocrites came down.
Hypocrites stayed behind from the Prophet's battles, then made excuses and oaths wanting praise for what they had not done, and a verse warning of painful chastisement was revealed.
Ibn Abbas told Marwan the verse on loving undeserved praise concerned People of the Book, who hid what the Prophet asked them, told him something else, and rejoiced.
